featureDevelopment.title: Security Tooling & Detection Engineering Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Threat Modeling: Requirement originates from CISO threat briefings, new CVE disclosures, or MITRE gap analyses.
2. Triage & Scoping: SOC Operations Manager assesses defensive priority, verifies telemetry sources, and approves ticket.
3. Analyst Assignment: Manager assigns the detection rule or automation script to the designated security engineer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Manager requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) before detection scripting begins.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: Security Engineer commits to a specific ETA, logged onto the SOC command board.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If detection rules or telemetry ingestion lag behind the ETA, Manager intervenes, clears SIEM access barriers, and accelerates completion.
7. Implementation & Testing: Engineer writes modular Sigma/YARA rules, accompanies changes with synthetic attack tests, and opens a PR.
8. Peer Review: Lead Security Architect reviews rule syntax and checks for potential false-positive noise.

9. Red Team QA Verification Gate: Red Team executes atomic tests simulating the adversary technique. If rule fails to fire, Red Team reports back to Manager with PCAP traces; if successful, sign-off is granted.
10. Production Deployment: SecOps Lead pushes rule to SIEM/EDR endpoints and activates automated containment webhooks.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: Vulnerability Discovery, Incident Triage, and Containment Lifecycle
steps: 1. Incident Discovery: Red team audit, internal scanner, or external telemetry flags an active vulnerability or IOC breach.
2. QA Vulnerability Report: Security analyst files an emergency incident ticket detailing affected host, CVSS score, PoC exploit, and containment recommendations submitted to SOC Manager.
3. Management Triage: SOC Operations Manager assesses blast radius, declares incident severity, and dispatches to SecOps/Engineering leads.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Manager demands an immediate containment ETA (sub-15 minute target).
5. Continuous Follow-Up: Manager monitors containment progress minute-by-minute; if ETA slips, escalates to CISO and deploys emergency isolation.
6. Remediation Implementation: Engineers revoke compromised credentials, isolate affected containers, and patch root vulnerabilities.
7. Re-Testing Verification: Red Team re-runs exploit against the patched endpoint to verify complete mitigation.
8. Post-Mortem Rollout: Manager records lessons learned into facts.md/procedural.md and closes the security incident.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time Security Codebase & Attack Surface Exploration Protocol
steps: 1. CISO Architecture Discovery: CISO explores repository topology, authentication mechanisms, API routes, dependency trees, and network egress rules.
2. Threat Surface Memorization: CISO records critical attack surfaces, credential locations, and IAM trust boundaries into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: CISO breaks defense into Auth, Network Security, Detection Rules, and CI/CD Security, delegating to Managers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: SOC Operations Manager inspects firewall configurations and procedures, recording them in procedural.md.
5. Specialist Deep-Dive: Security engineers inspect assigned scripts, run static analysis (Semgrep, Trivy), and verify log ingestion pipelines.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All analysts record verified IOCs, CVE patches, and remediation recipes into facts.md and procedural.md.

leadershipRules.title: Strict Security Command Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: CISO and SOC Operations Managers NEVER write detection scripts, edit firewall rules, or perform hands-on remediation directly.
Command leadership orchestrates threat response, enforces containment ETAs, coordinates legal/compliance, and manages team execution.
When asked to write code, command leadership explains the cybersecurity chain of command and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
